headline: Dealing with a Stubborn Drain Clog that Won't Budge
articleBody:
It's super frustrating when a drain just won't clear, no matter how much plunging you do. A stubborn drain clog can slow down your daily routine and even lead to bigger plumbing problems if ignored. Whether it's your kitchen sink, shower, or even a toilet that keeps backing up, these clogs often indicate more than just a simple blockage right at the surface. In the Las Vegas Valley, we see all sorts of stubborn clogs, from hair and grease buildup to mineral deposits and even tree roots.

**Common Mistakes to Avoid**
When you're faced with a clog that won't budge, it's easy to make a few common mistakes that can actually make things worse. First, repeatedly flushing an overflowing toilet or continuing to run water into a backed-up sink is a big no-no – it just adds to the overflow and potential water damage. Another common one is using harsh chemical drain cleaners. While they promise quick fixes, they can damage your pipes, especially older ones, and they're really bad for the environment. Plus, if a professional then needs to come in, those chemicals can create a hazardous situation for the plumber. FEMA advises against using chemicals before professional service. Also, never combine different chemical cleaners; that can create dangerous fumes or reactions. Lastly, if you're tempted to try a drain snake yourself, be careful. Without the right technique, you could push the clog further, scratch your pipes, or even get the snake stuck.

Before professional service, ensure no one is using other fixtures. If raw sewage or wastewater is present, keep people and pets away from the affected area to prevent contamination. This is especially important for main drain issues. Stopping the water flow is critical to preventing further damage and health risks. A single slow drain might allow for a bit of basic troubleshooting, but if sewage is present or multiple fixtures are affected, it’s best to avoid any DIY attempts and call in an expert.
